title: 5 prompts to clear your inbox faster

sources.name: Prompting guidance: state the task, audience and tone

caption:
5 prompts for the email jobs that eat your day: triage, quick replies, polite declines, follow-ups and clearer subject lines.
Remove private details before pasting, and always read the draft before you send it.
Save this for your next full inbox. Comment INBOX and I will send the prompt list.

slides.headline: Remove private details first
body: Swap names and sensitive facts for placeholders before pasting.

slides.headline: Triage the pile
body: Paste only the parts you need sorted.
slides.prompt: Sort these emails into: needs a reply today, needs a reply this week, and no reply needed. Give a one-line reason for each. [emails]

slides.headline: Write the quick reply
slides.prompt: Draft a two-sentence reply to [message]. Answer the question directly and keep the tone friendly and professional.

slides.headline: Decline politely
body: Say no clearly without sounding cold.
slides.prompt: Write a polite decline to [request]. Thank them, give one short reason, and suggest [alternative] if it fits.

slides.headline: Follow up without nagging
body: A gentle nudge that makes the next step clear.
slides.prompt: Write a brief follow-up to [message] sent [days] ago. Restate the ask in one sentence and make it easy to reply.

slides.headline: Fix the subject line
body: Clear subjects get opened and answered.
slides.prompt: Give me five clear subject lines for an email about [topic]. Each under eight words. Do not use all caps.

slides.headline: Edit it to sound like you
body: Remove stiff phrases and add your usual greeting.
slides.prompt: Rewrite this draft in a warmer, more casual tone. Keep the facts and the request unchanged.

slides.headline: Read it once, out loud
body: Make sure the ask is obvious.

slides.headline: Save this inbox toolkit
body: Comment INBOX and I will send the prompt list.
Share this with someone drowning in email.
